why.title: The idea
why.text: 21.Bxg7!! gives up the bishop on g7 to stay in the game: after it White holds the balance (0.00); anything else leaves White losing (−3.21).

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: 21.Bxg7 puts the bishop on g7 where it can be taken by the king. That's a bishop on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the bishop
why.text: 21…Kxg7 is met by 22.Qg5+. Then 23.Rh8+ gives check, and 24.Rxg8# is mate.

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the bishop alone and play 21…d2. White answers 22.g4, threatening Bxf6, winning a knight. Then 23.Bxf6 takes the knight on f6, and 24.Kg2 threatens mate. White is a piece down: White holds the balance (0.00).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 21.f4, is clearly weaker (−3.21 against 0.00). Black answers 21…Qc8, threatening …Qxf5, winning the queen. That would leave White losing.

moments.name: 21…d2
moments.headline: 21…d2!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Leaves the knight on f6 where it can be taken.

Pushes the passed pawn to d2, close to promotion.
21…d2 threatens …Re1+, with mate in 2, and stops the mate threat Bxf6.
It threatens …Re1+, with mate in 2, so White has to spend the next move on it.
White was threatening Bxf6, with mate in 4. d2 takes care of it.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 21…d2!! gives up the pawn on d2 to stay in the game: after it Black holds the balance (+0.09); anything else leaves Black getting mated (#5).

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: The knight on f6 is attacked by the rook on d1, and 21…d2 doesn't save it. That's a pawn on offer.

why.title: If White takes the pawn
why.text: 22.Rxd2 is met by 22…Re1#, and it's mate.

why.title: If White takes the knight
why.text: 22.Bxf6 is met by 22…Re1+, and the rook on e7 gets away. Then 23…dxe1=Q# is mate.

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the pawn alone and play 22.g3. Black answers 22…Re1+. Then 23…Kxg7 takes the bishop on g7, and 25…Ke8 threatens …Rxd1, winning a rook. Black is a pawn down: Black holds the balance (+0.09).

why.title: Why not save the knight first?
why.text: Saving it with 21…Nh5, the best way to do that, is clearly weaker (#5 against +0.09). White answers 22.Rxh5, taking the knight on h5 and threatening Qh7# and mate. That would leave Black getting mated.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 25.Qxf6!! ignores the attack on the rook on d1 and takes the knight on f6 first. Taking the rook leads to mate.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: The rook on d1 is attacked by the rook on e1, and 25.Qxf6 doesn't save it. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It takes the knight on f6 first.

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the rook alone and play 25…Ke8. White answers 26.Rh8+. Then 27.Rxd2 takes the d2 pawn. White ends up a piece and a pawn ahead: White holds the balance (+0.30).
